This memorandum addresses the enforceability of the forum selection and arbitration clauses in the contract between Meridian Technologies Inc. and Apex Global Solutions LLC. Based on analysis of controlling case law in the 9th Circuit and federal statutes, forum selection and arbitration clauses are generally enforceable if they are clear, unambiguous, and not contrary to public policy. The contract at issue specifies Delaware law and mandates arbitration in Wilmington, DE, which is likely enforceable under federal policy favoring arbitration (9 U.S.C. and FAA precedent). However, equitable considerations may arise if enforcement would lead to undue hardship or waiver. Recent case law, including cases with comparable procedural postures, supports enforcement absent a strong showing of inconvenience or unfairness. We recommend proceeding with the opposition to the Motion to Dismiss on other grounds while preserving the right to compel arbitration if necessary.

This memorandum addresses the enforceability of the forum selection clause in the contract between Meridian Technologies Inc. and Apex Global Solutions LLC. Based on Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(b)(6) and controlling precedent such as *Ashcroft v. Iqbal*, a forum selection clause is generally enforceable unless the opposing party can show it is unreasonable or unjust. The clause in question, which designates Wilmington, DE as the exclusive forum, aligns with the governing law provision under Delaware law and appears reasonable given the parties' commercial relationship. No controlling case law invalidating similar clauses in this jurisdiction was identified. However, the clause may be challenged on grounds of unequal bargaining power or lack of notice, though such arguments are unlikely to succeed absent evidence of fraud or overreach. We recommend proceeding on the basis that the clause is enforceable, which supports venue in Delaware federal court.
